native: One Tuesday in June, teacher Laura Ortiz welcomes Jorge Medina and his son Mateo in room 12 to review the portfolio from the school year.
Ms. Ortiz: Mr. Medina, look how much Mateo's writing has grown.
Ms. Ortiz: Compare this story from September with the one from May.
In the first writing sample, Mateo wrote 3 short sentences, and in the last one he wrote 2 pages with a beginning, middle and end.
The teacher explains that the growth also shows in his spelling, because Mateo now checks his words before turning in his homework.
Then she shows the father the self-assessment Mateo filled out in May, where he chose his own goals for the summer.
Ms. Ortiz: Mateo, which piece of work makes you feel proudest?
Mateo: The story about the dog, because I read it aloud in front of the whole class.
Ms. Ortiz: He would be ready for fourth grade, as long as he keeps reading.
Next she presents the summer plan, in which Mateo would go to the district summer camp in the mornings and read at home in the afternoons.
Ms. Ortiz: If he read 20 minutes a day, he would keep his level.
She also suggests getting a card at the public library, which has a reading program in June and July.
Jorge: Are the hearing supports going to continue next year?
Ms. Ortiz: The hearing supports in his plan would continue in fourth grade, unless the team decides otherwise.
Ms. Ortiz: I'll pass on his file so his fourth-grade teacher knows his supports.
Ms. Ortiz: I would recommend requesting the plan's annual review before August.
Ms. Ortiz: If you notice any changes in his hearing, let us know.
Jorge leaves proud with the portfolio under his arm and promises to take Mateo to the public library every Saturday.

passage.title: Día de examen sin suplente
target: Hoy es el día de examen en la Primaria Lincoln, y en el salón 110 el aplicador del examen es el maestro Daniel Ríos.
Antes de empezar, Daniel entrena a la asistente Rosa Delgado en la nueva estación de escritura, adonde van los niños que terminan el examen.
Daniel: Rosa, obsérvame primero y después explícamelo tú.
Rosa explica que primero guarda el cuadernillo de examen de cada niño y revisa que la hoja de respuestas tenga su nombre.
Daniel: Bien, y si un niño se atora, no le des la respuesta; dale una pista.
A las 9:15, la oficina avisa que el salón 112 no tiene suplente, y Daniel recibe al grupo sin maestro.
Daniel: Los del salón 112, siéntense en las mesas del fondo, por favor.
A las 10:00, Rosa ve ronchas en el cuello de Nico y nota que tiene el labio hinchado.
Daniel: Nico, ¿sientes comezón en la boca o te cuesta respirar?
Nico dice que tiene comezón pero respira bien, y que comió una galleta de cacahuate que le dio un compañero.
Daniel saca el plan de alergias de Nico y llama por el intercomunicador: Oficina, aquí salón 110; necesito a la enfermera ahora mismo.

La enfermera llega enseguida y atiende a Nico según su plan de alergias: si el plan lo indica, usa la epinefrina, la oficina llama al 911 y la enfermera llama a sus papás, mientras Rosa cuida el examen.
A la 1:30, un familiar llega por Sofía, la hija de Inés Cordero, pero no está en la lista ni trae credencial.
Daniel: Lo siento, no le puedo entregar a la niña sin autorización.
Daniel llama a la mamá por teléfono: Señora Cordero, ¿podría venir a la oficina para autorizarlo por escrito?
Por la tarde, Daniel escribe el informe del día y lo lleva al director, el Dr. Martín Esquivel.
Daniel: Doctor Esquivel, le resumo el día en orden cronológico, y a continuación le entrego la línea de tiempo.
Daniel: Cabe señalar que el examen no se interrumpió en ningún momento y que la persona no autorizada no se llevó a Sofía.
native: Today is testing day at Lincoln Elementary, and in room 110 the test proctor is the teacher Daniel Ríos.
Before starting, Daniel trains the aide Rosa Delgado at the new writing station, where the children who finish the test go.
Daniel: Rosa, watch me first and then explain it back to me.
Rosa explains that first she puts away each child's test booklet and checks that the answer sheet has his or her name.
Daniel: Good, and if a child gets stuck, don't give him the answer; give him a hint.
At 9:15, the office announces that room 112 has no sub, and Daniel takes in the class with no teacher.
Daniel: Room 112, please sit at the tables in the back.
At 10:00, Rosa sees hives on Nico's neck and notices that he has a swollen lip.
Daniel: Nico, does your mouth itch or is it hard to breathe?
Nico says that he has itching but is breathing fine, and that he ate a peanut cookie that a classmate gave him.
Daniel takes out Nico's allergy plan and calls on the intercom: Office, this is room 110; I need the nurse right now.

The nurse arrives right away and treats Nico according to his allergy plan: if the plan calls for it, she uses the epinephrine, the office calls 911, and the nurse calls his parents, while Rosa watches the test.
At 1:30, a relative arrives to pick up Sofía, Inés Cordero's daughter, but he is not on the list and does not have an ID card.
Daniel: I'm sorry, I can't release the girl to you without authorization.
Daniel calls the mom on the phone: Mrs. Cordero, could you come to the office to authorize it in writing?
In the afternoon, Daniel writes the end-of-day report and takes it to the principal, Dr. Martín Esquivel.
Daniel: Dr. Esquivel, I'll summarize the day for you in chronological order, and next I'll hand you the timeline.
Daniel: It should be noted that the test was never interrupted and that the unauthorized person did not take Sofía.
